per_column.name: narrative_structure_issue
per_column.rationale: Categorising narrative/plot problems gives a genuine axis for explaining dissatisfaction. Values are conservative (mostly not_present) and defensible for the sampled rows; no clear contradictions observed.

per_column.name: originality_or_novelty
per_column.rationale: Formulaic/derivative/clichéd is a useful dimension for dissatisfaction. Row IMDB-0002 tagged 'derivative' has little source support (review stresses badness, not derivativeness), a mild overreach; other rows (formulaic for housewife/soap-opera premise) are well grounded.

per_column.name: tone_or_consistency_issue
per_column.rationale: Tone/consistency is a distinct, useful axis. 'mismatched_attempted_appeal' for the positive sexploitation review (IMDB-0004) is a stretch since that review is favourable; 'wrong_genre_fit' labels are plausible readings of the daytime-movie/technobabble complaints.

per_column.name: genre_audience_mismatch
per_column.rationale: Genre/audience mismatch is a meaningful grouping axis. 'inappropriate_for_audience' for the housewife-movie row is well grounded, but 'marketed_vs_delivered_genre' for IMDB-0001 is not clearly supported by the text (no marketing claim mentioned).

per_column.name: reliance_on_clich_s
per_column.rationale: Overlaps somewhat with originality_or_novelty (clichés vs formulaic) reducing marginal leverage, but the sub-typing (plot device/theme/characters) still adds detail. 'overused_theme' for IMDB-0005, a broadly positive review, is weakly supported.

judge.rationale: The added columns decompose reasons for dissatisfaction into distinct, groupable dimensions (structure, originality, tone, genre fit, clichés) directly serving the query; each gives an analytical axis rather than being trivial or near-constant, though originality and reliance_on_clichés partly overlap. Values are generally conservative and defensible readings of the source text, but several sampled rows show unwarranted specifics ('marketed_vs_delivered_genre', 'derivative', 'mismatched_attempted_appeal' and 'overused_theme' applied to positive reviews) that the text does not clearly support, indicating occasional but not pervasive hallucination.
